This quiz will focus on data frame manipulation, however, you may need to rely on skills you've learned in prior weeks. 

1. load the starwars dataset from tidyverse
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data("starwars")
```


2. separate the films column so that there is one film in each column (don't worry about the "c(" and ) at the end for now)

```{r}
colnames(starwars)
print(starwars$films)

starwars <- starwars %>% separate(films, into = c("Film 1", "Film 2", "Film 3", "Film 4", "Film 5", "Film 6"), sep = ",")

```



3. alter the data from wide data to long data
```{r}
library(reshape2)
library(dplyr)
summarise(starwars)

starwars_long<- starwars %>% mutate(mass = as.character(mass), height = as.character(height), birth_year = as.character(birth_year), vehicles = as.character(vehicles), starships = as.character(starships)) %>%pivot_longer(cols = colnames(starwars)[2:19], names_to = "Characteristics", values_to = "Details", values_drop_na = TRUE)
```


4. in the column where you stored the films, rename the levels so each film name is consistent (e.g. get rid of the "c(" and ")" )
```{r}
library(stringr)
colnames(starwars_long)

starwars_long <- starwars_long%>%mutate(Details = as.factor(Details))


starwars_long<- starwars_long%>%mutate(Details = as.character(Details)%>% str_remove_all('c\\("')%>%str_remove_all('\\)')%>%str_remove_all('"')%>%as.factor())


starwars_long$Details<- relevel(starwars_long$Details, ref = "A New Hope")
levels(starwars_long$Details)

```
#I searched how to use slash \\ and how to use the str_remove_all() function.


5. Create a column in your dataset that indicates whether a character was in the first starwars film, *Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope* 
```{r}
#This is starwars_long version but I could not figure out (i.e., I could only detect the rows that contained "A New Hope" TRUE, but not all rows for each character who appeared in that film. ). I am also not sure if I understand this question correctly.

starwars_long<- starwars_long%>%mutate(A_New_Hope = Details == "A New Hope")


#I used the wide version and figured out the way to add new column "A New Hope" that correctly indicates 'yes' for characters who appeared in the film. 

colnames(starwars)

starwars<- starwars%>%mutate(`Film 1`= as.character(`Film 1`)%>%str_remove_all('c\\("')%>%str_remove_all('"')%>%as.factor())

starwars<- starwars%>%mutate(A_New_Hope = ifelse(`Film 1` == "A New Hope"|`Film 2` == "A New Hope"|`Film 3` == "A New Hope"|`Film 4` == "A New Hope"| `Film 5` == "A New Hope"|`Film 6` == "A New Hope", "Yes")) 
```

6. BMI is calculated as mass in Kg/height in meters squared. You currently have mass in Kg and height in cm. Create a column that contains each character's BMI. 
```{r}
#Just a note: BMI = mass / (height/100)^2   cm --> meters 165/100= 1.65

starwars<- starwars%>%mutate(BMI = mass/(height/100)^2)
```
#I translated the question, and AI translator answered me "BMIは、体重(kg)を身長(m)の2乗で割って算出します。"


7. create a dataframe that contains only the name, hair color, and eye color for each character. 
```{r}
#Used wide version.
name_hair_eye_info<- starwars %>% select(name, hair_color, eye_color)


#Long version
info_longdataver<- starwars_long%>%filter(Characteristics== "hair_color"|Characteristics == "eye_color")
info_longdataver<- info_longdataver[, -4] #Just delete the fourth column

```
